svg.title: Atoms, isotopes & models
svg.desc: Nucleus & charge: Protons +1 and neutrons 0 each have relative mass 1. Electrons −1 have tiny mass. Atomic number = protons. Neutrons = mass number − atomic number. Na-23: 11p, 12n, 11e. Na⁺: 11p, 12n, 10e. Size & isotope averages: Atom radius ≈ 10⁻¹⁰ m; nucleus ≈ 10⁻¹⁴ m or less. Almost all mass is nuclear. 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m. Isotopes: same protons, different neutrons. Aᵣ weights each isotope by abundance. 75% mass 35 + 25% mass 37 → 35.5. Shells & position: Lowest shells fill first: 2,8,8,2 for first 20 elements. O: 2,6; Na: 2,8,1; Ca: 2,8,8,2. Period = occupied shells. Same main group = same outer electrons → similar reactions. Metals generally lose electrons; non-metals gain/share. Atoms → ions: Losing negative electrons produces a positive ion; gaining them produces a negative ion. The number of protons stays unchanged: it remains the same element. Full outer shells help explain the stability of noble gases. Scattering conclusions: Most alpha particles pass → atom mostly empty space. Some deflect → nucleus is positive and repels positive alpha particles. Very few return → tiny, dense nucleus holds most mass; contradicts spread-out positive charge. Changing models: Indivisible spheres → discovery of electron → plum pudding. Scattering → nuclear model. Bohr: specific electron shells. Later work: protons. Chadwick: neutrons. New experimental evidence can replace a scientific model.
